learningObjective: Reason about the arithmetic intensity of a tiled GEMM kernel and why larger tiles increase compute-per-byte until register/SMEM pressure caps the design.

canonicalClaims.claim: For a tiled GEMM with block tile M_TILE x N_TILE and K-step K_TILE, arithmetic intensity per byte of A/B fetched scales as (M_TILE*N_TILE)/(M_TILE+N_TILE), bounded above by on-chip storage.
conditions: A and B fragments are staged in SMEM and reused across all threads in the block.
The accumulator C_TILE lives in registers or SMEM within a single thread block.
nonImplications: Does not imply that arbitrarily large tiles are optimal; register spill and reduced occupancy dominate past a threshold.
Does not imply that intensity alone determines runtime; launch config, tensor cores, and dtype also matter.

misconceptions.claim: Arithmetic intensity of GEMM is independent of tile size; tiling only changes the launch grid.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Without tiling every output would re-fetch A/B rows/columns from HBM; tiling raises the reuse factor and directly cuts HBM traffic per output.

misconceptions.claim: Setting K_TILE = K in one step is always optimal for HBM traffic minimization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: K is often too large to fit; K_TILE is chosen to fit A and B fragments into SMEM. HBM traffic per flop is dominated by M_TILE/N_TILE-driven reuse, not by K_TILE.

misconceptions.claim: C write traffic dominates GEMM HBM cost, so larger tiles reduce arithmetic intensity.
misconceptions.whyWrong: C writes are O(M*N) while A*B fetch/compute is much larger; larger tiles increase reuse and intensity, not decrease.

misconceptions.claim: Bigger tiles are always better because they raise arithmetic intensity monotonically.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Beyond register/SMEM capacity, spills and reduced occupancy hurt throughput; tile sizing is a bounded optimization.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA Best Practices Guide — occupancy vs tile

implementationFacts: Typical A100 SGEMM/HGEMM CTA tiles are 128x128 with K_TILE = 32 or 64.
Accumulator tile size drives register usage per thread; too large → spills.
performanceScenarios: Skinny GEMMs (small M or N) benefit from imbalanced tiles because the smaller dim caps intensity.
FP16/BF16 with FP32 accumulate on tensor cores changes the per-op intensity but the tile-sizing intuition remains.
